choice: Represent two lumped parallel reactions in the reactor: desired CO2 + 3H2 -> CH3OH + H2O and undesired reverse water-gas shift CO2 + H2 -> CO + H2O; use each record's carbon selectivity to partition converted CO2, with methanol and CO as the only carbon products.
alternatives: Single desired reaction with selectivity treated only as a yield penalty
Include methane, DME and higher oxygenates explicitly
reason: The extracted papers consistently evaluate methanol against CO from RWGS, while the heterogeneous catalyst families have different proposed surface intermediates that cannot be parameterized consistently across 124 records. The two-reaction carbon balance preserves the dominant process consequences of selectivity: extra H2 consumption, CO purge, water production and reduced methanol yield.

choice: Infer an apparent far-from-equilibrium methanol productivity from each lab record using r0 = r_lab/(1-X_lab/Xeq_lab), then predict plant productivity at candidate per-pass conversion as r = r0*(1-X/Xeq) at the record temperature, pressure and fresh-feed ratio; constrain X below equilibrium and optimize X against catalyst inventory, recycle/compression and separation. Apply reported 10%-activity-loss cycle time to replacement and average-in-cycle inventory; otherwise use a sourced catalyst-life uncertainty.
alternatives: Use reported productivity unchanged at every plant conversion
Fit one universal power-law or Langmuir-Hinshelwood model across all catalyst families
Scale rate only with Arrhenius temperature and pressure exponents
Assume plant conversion equals reported laboratory conversion
reason: A universal detailed rate law is not identifiable from heterogeneous one-point literature records. The approach-to-equilibrium correction retains the measured catalyst-specific productivity while enforcing thermodynamic slowdown and lets the plant choose conversion. It is conservative near equilibrium and avoids rewarding tests merely run at low conversion.

choice: Use an industrial multitubular cooled fixed-bed reactor operated at each literature record's temperature and pressure, with boiling-water heat removal; optimize per-pass CO2 conversion below equilibrium rather than forcing the lab conversion.
reason: Methanol synthesis is strongly exothermic and equilibrium-limited, so controlled heat removal avoids hot spots and preserves methanol selectivity. A cooled packed bed is compatible with the solid powder-derived catalysts after industrial shaping and permits catalyst inventory to scale from measured productivity.

choice: Cool and knock out methanol/water, recycle uncondensed CO2/H2 with a CO purge, and distill the condensed crude liquid to 99.9 mol% methanol; estimate duties from stream-dependent condensation and a sourced specific distillation-energy range.
reason: Methanol and water are condensable while CO2, H2 and CO remain predominantly gaseous after cooling, enabling conventional gas recycle. Distillation is needed because the condensed reaction product contains stoichiometric water and methanol purity must be enforced.

choice: Set a gate-to-gate synthesis-island boundary from separate pressurized CO2 and H2 feeds to stored on-spec liquid methanol, including feed compression, recycle, reactor, cooling, purification, product pumping and offsites; price upstream CO2 and H2 at the boundary and discharge purge gas and aqueous bottoms.
alternatives: Include CO2 capture and purification plant
reason: The requested question is which catalyst an industrial methanol plant would choose. Holding upstream supply technologies outside the battery limit permits catalyst records to be compared on a common process while retaining feedstock-cost attenuation through fixed transfer prices.

choice: Calculate finished-catalyst purchase cost as the fixed support/manufacturing price plus elemental metal price times reported catalyst weight fraction; when a paper names components but omits loadings, distribute a total 10 wt% active-component proxy equally among priced named elements, with 1–30 wt% sensitivity.
alternatives: Assign one identical catalyst price to every record
Infer oxide stoichiometry and full formulation from catalyst names
Use density-functional adsorption energies to predict catalyst cost or activity
Exclude every record lacking complete weight fractions
reason: The extracted literature is inconsistent in reporting active loadings, but catalyst replacement and noble-metal exposure must remain visible. The proxy uses only the fixed price table and reported composition while placing the unsupported loading assumption under deterministic sensitivity.
